ChildReference.description: Select one exact child request in this proposal. The request maps to a complete retained Plan; a UUID without that binding is not an executable target.

RequestBinding.description: One exact child request with a complete reviewed Plan, assigned to an installed procedure phase. Initial ready Plans are the first request for their participant and use its initial expected_generation. Later reviewed Plans are retained through workflow.bind, with current independently verified preconditions. The Plan owner and subject resource match its participant; every effect remains within the immutable participant closure. adapter.execute requires the complete approved AdapterInput; other actions forbid it.

HostDrainTarget.description: The exact host change whose reviewed Plan binds disruption, live scope and recovery. Participant Plans contain all admitted application draining and reconciliation work.

InterfaceBindingTarget.description: The exact typed application provider deployment, upgrade or repair Plan and each intended consumer Plan bind the reviewed interface configuration through their retained release/input material. Native phase admission verifies the produced binding and each consumer obligation.

IngressPublicationTarget.description: The publication child is adapter.execute with the exact approved ingress executor and fishhat.ingress publish AdapterInput, retaining complete candidate routes and expected generation. An unrelated mutation method cannot satisfy this role.

SecretRotationTarget.description: The ready issuer_change is the exact credential-issuer issue child. publication is a secret-publication continuation for that issuer, in the installed publishing phase. Every consumer_adoption is a secret-adoption continuation referring to those same issuer and publisher children. Real output material is bound only after it exists and is independently verified, reviewed and retained. Preparation never invents a future receipt.

CheckpointTarget.description: The exact capture Plan, including the accepted source and complete native data/secret/release recovery inputs. Capture is distinct from a successful restore drill.

RelocationTarget.description: The exact relocation Plan binds the source application identity, destination, fencing and checkpoint or release recovery basis.

SourcePublicationTarget.description: The exact source.publish Plan binds the intended source, base and complete proposal content before a client can disappear.

DnsChangeTarget.description: The exact dns.reconcile Plan binds the complete changeset and approved provider scope.

SecretPublicationTarget.description: The exact publisher publication or recovery Plan binds the immutable secret candidate and selected predecessor.

RawMaintenanceTarget.description: The exact reviewed maintenance Plan binds the admitted task or approved adapter method, its scope, expected disruption and reconciliation. This target is not a caller-supplied command or procedure graph.

RuntimeUpgradeTarget.description: The exact host.runtime-install Plan binds the management release, selected tools and state-preserving migration scope.

WorkflowProposal.description: The immutable installed procedure, participant/resource closure, initial driver agreement and child request slots. A ready child retains its complete reviewed Plan and material; a closed continuation intent retains exact scope, predecessor and allowed action without inventing future material or a stale future Plan. Every receiver independently authorizes the full local closure and initial driver, and pins existing local content before preparation. Other participants retain the same proposal digest. Later reviewed Plans and actual output material are attached only by workflow.bind under current authority and exact retained lineage; this does not edit the proposal or admit a child effect. Stored initial intent and accepted bindings survive client loss, transfer and recovery. Procedure phase order is installed, never caller-defined.

PrepareRequest.description: The complete decoded preparation payload. The selected receiver is a participant and independently approves the immutable initial_driver assignment. A transport caller never implicitly becomes driver. Repeating the exact workflow_id and proposal under current permission returns retained custody, including any transferred driver; changed intent conflicts. Fresh local content, approval and current admission checks precede preparation. Generation starts at zero and initial driver term at one; no child effect is accepted.

TransferCompletion.description: The full independently authenticated commit closure. Every distinct participant owner appears exactly once with state transferred, the original proposal digest and workflow ID. The local witness equals the receiving owner retained commit; another signature, later generation, substitute epoch or omitted owner does not complete this transfer.

AdvanceRequest.description: One immutable advance identity. The receiving owner reauthorizes the actual principal, resolves advance_id and exact retained input before current generation/term or new-input expiry checks, and replays an identical accepted transition without executing it again. Changed input under the same advance_id conflicts. A new request compares the exact local capsule generation and current driver term and follows the installed next phase; it cannot skip phases or revive terminal/recovery-required work. Every prerequisite witness is independently authenticated and checked against its local procedure obligations. When a transfer is pending in commit phase, transfer_completion must contain the complete transferred-witness closure for the exact proposal and the unchanged retained local commit. The owner atomically retains that evidence, marks the transfer completed, records the advance outcome and increments its capsule generation once. Transfer completion must preserve the current procedure phase and exact lifecycle state; subsequent phase progress requires a separate ordinarily authorized advance. It never implies rollback, release of holds or completion of a child operation. An unavailable epoch or incomplete evidence remains unresolved and cannot be replaced by timeout. Driver transfer is orthogonal to lifecycle. Completion preserves the exact prior lifecycle state, including paused and recovery-required. No transfer is permitted to reactivate cancelled or completed work. A successor with recovery preparation not yet committed cannot advance.

AdvanceReceipt.description: The original complete accepted advance and its immutable finite outcome, not a recursive Workflow snapshot. generation is the local atomic transition generation and remains fixed after later advances or transfers. The capsule retains these receipts so another authorized caller can reconstruct exact replay without client files. A replay returns the current capsule containing this original receipt and never reapplies the transition.

InputReference.description: The sole wire input shape for workflow.prepare, workflow.bind, workflow.advance, workflow.transfer and workflow.recover. Complete canonical-JSON payloads are staged through content.begin/chunk/commit under resource {kind: workflow, id: workflow_id}; the RPC carries only this bounded immutable reference. The method owns the payload schema: PrepareRequest, BindRequest, AdvanceRequest, records.WorkflowTransferRequest or workflow-recovery.RecoveryRequest respectively. No caller-selected schema, inline alternate, subset or truncated witness closure is accepted. Verify complete bytes, digest, size, exact owner epoch, protected staging scope and current principal before interpreting the payload. Resolve a previously retained exact semantic request before new-admission expiry checks; original accepted content remains pinned. An authorized replacement caller may restage the identical canonical request: the handle is a transport locator, while the decoded immutable request defines replay identity. New requests require fresh committed custody and independently approved receiving capacity. Chunk bounds do not bound the complete proposal or evidence set. Before acknowledgment the receiving owner authorizes every participant resource it owns and retains the decoded original input plus all needed content. These declarations do not implement staging, native authorization or persistence.

AdapterInput.description: Exact receiving-owner-approved selected executor and complete typed mutation planning input. The executor role equals the request contract and its scope equals request.input.scope. The child Plan adapter_id, adapter_release and action equal the executor instance, installation digest and request method. Its input handle contains canonical request bytes, with matching digest and size; input_schema_digest pins the complete installed role schema closure rooted at MutationRequest and result_schema pins the same role Output. The receiver independently checks this binding, method support, configuration, grants and native controlling authority against protected approved enrollment before preparation; supplied identity data never approves or enrolls an adapter. Child admission still requires its own owner-authored Invocation and current authorization. This input does not create or dispatch an effect. installation_digest and adapter_release identify the immutable artifact key used by approved Installation; descriptor and configuration approval are separate protected owner facts.

InitialDriver.description: The immutable initial driver agreement shared by all participant owners. The caller transporting preparation need not be this principal. Each receiver independently authorizes this exact assignment against protected local policy; the proposal is not a delegation grant. Accepted replay preserves the retained driver and any later transfer.

oneOf.description: A later reviewed Plan for this exact subject, after the immediately preceding request on the same participant succeeds with known effects. This declares ordering inside an installed phase sequence, never a caller-defined procedure graph. Fresh Plan preconditions, review and custody are required after the predecessor; initial generations are not reused.

Publish the actual complete ciphertext candidate produced from the exact successful issuer child. The selected publisher is this participant; source, entry, consumer, immutable version, catalogue digest and expected_previous are immutable. The candidate does not exist at preparation and is admitted only with an independently verified ProducedMaterial binding, complete content custody and a new reviewed publisher.publish Plan. This output intent may only be the first request for its participant. Every later request must be a reviewed-successor tied to the immediately preceding successful child, so two output slots cannot bind against one unchanged resource generation.

Adopt only the bundle produced by this workflow exact issuer and publication children. The later Plan pins the real completed publication receipt and retained ciphertext closure, with independently verified producer lineage and local material custody; a preexisting or unrelated receipt cannot fill this intent. This output intent may only be the first request for its participant. Every later request must be a reviewed-successor tied to the immediately preceding successful child, so two output slots cannot bind against one unchanged resource generation.

DeferredBinding.description: An immutable request slot requiring later owner-reviewed Plan binding. It is not a Plan, accepted operation or fabricated material handle. The installed procedure and declared predecessor constrain when it can be bound. A phase cannot finish with unresolved required slots. Secret-output intents are first-only; later participant requests always use reviewed-successor ordering.

ProducedMaterial.description: An independently verified material derivation retained by its receiving custodian. The witness owner equals material.owner, kind binding, state verified, exact workflow ID, and subject_digest covers the complete canonical body excluding witness. For publication, producer is the exact succeeded issuer operation and material is the complete ciphertext candidate derived from its issued credential. For adoption, producer is the exact succeeded publication operation, material contains the complete publication receipt, and that receipt names the exact published candidate and custodian. A receiver independently authenticates this lineage and byte custody before placing it in verified_materials; neither a signature-shaped object nor the request supplies that approval. The issuer-to-publication binding is retained transitively, never replaced by a coincidental receipt digest. producer_output is a verified receiving-custodian copy of the exact non-null Operation result handle bytes, matching digest and size and retained in the new Plan input closure. For adoption it equals material and therefore the canonical receipt is the exact publication Operation output, not another publication of equal ciphertext.

BindRequest.description: One exact later-reviewed child binding. The receiver resolves bind_id replay before freshness, checks the immutable slot and installed phase, current driver, authentic complete predecessor evidence and the protected current resource generations, then independently approves the full new Plan. Every material and selected adapter is verified and retained before acknowledgment. Input is staged through workflow-input custody. The binding atomically increments only the local workflow capsule generation and retains its original request; it does not admit native effects. Plan admission still checks current owner/resource generation, deadline and permission. The same child cannot acquire a different Plan. Other replicas retain the same owner-approved binding and producer lineage under their own exact local request identity; transport alone supplies no approval.

BindReceipt.description: The complete accepted binding request and local committed capsule generation. Retained exact input supports replay after deadline, generation or driver changes; current access remains required. Binding receipts are append-only, unique by bind_id and child, and preserve preceding output lineage.

CompletedBinding.description: A nonexecutable successor slot fulfilled by an exact previously succeeded operation and its original Plan. The new slot identity is a workflow reference, never a new operation request. Original owner epoch, request identity, Plan and outcome remain unchanged. Only workflow.recover may introduce this slot after independently verifying the complete predecessor closure. A fresh prepare cannot turn a supplied receipt into fulfillment. Later continuations use the retained original successful operation as their predecessor evidence.
